Medical History

- Current health issues and chronic disease risk factors (e.g., hypertension, diabetes):
  • Acute localized reaction to recent wasp/bee sting on right arm; mild erythema/puncture mark.  
  • Reports transient sensation of breathing difficulty and slight lip/tongue “weird” feeling; clinician observed no airway compromise.  
  • Past history: eczema; occasional anxiety/panic attacks (never medicated).  
  • Drug allergy: penicillin.  
- Family history of chronic conditions (e.g., CVD, diabetes): Not recorded.
- Current medications including OTC and traditional medicines: None at time of consult. Clinician advised OTC antihistamine (chlorphenamine 4 mg up to 6×/day or once-daily alternative); dose/route/frequency to be determined by patient purchase.
- Immunisation status reviewed (flu, COVID-19, pneumococcal, shingles, tetanus): Not recorded.
- Sexual/reproductive health status and risks: Not recorded.
- Lifestyle: physical activity, diet, tobacco, alcohol, substance use: Not recorded.
- Hearing and vision concerns: Not recorded.
- Mood, mental health, and risk assessment (depression, anxiety, self-harm):
  • Occasional anxiety/panic attacks; no current treatment.  
  • No depressive symptoms or self-harm ideation discussed.
- Social context: family support, caregiving, housing, financial stressors:
  • Lives alone.  
  • Occupation: computer scientist.  
  • Has a pet cat.  
  • No financial or housing concerns raised.

Examination

- Vital signs: BP, pulse rate and rhythm: Not recorded.
- Anthropometry: height, weight, BMI, waist circumference if indicated: Not recorded.
- Oral health: gums, teeth, dentures if relevant: Brief visual inspection of oral cavity; no swelling of lips, tongue, or soft tissues observed.
- Ear exam including otoscopy: Not performed.
- Eye exam: visual acuity, pupil response, fundus if indicated: Not performed.
- Urinalysis: dipstick for protein, glucose, ketones, blood: Not performed.

Investigations (as indicated)

- Blood tests: None ordered.
- Renal function and liver function tests: Not indicated.
- ECG: Not indicated.
- Cervical screening: Not applicable/not discussed.
- Mammography: Not applicable/not discussed.
- Faecal occult blood test: Not discussed.
- Bone density (DEXA): Not discussed.

Health Promotion & Planning

- Education on chronic disease prevention and lifestyle modification:
  • Provided education on recognizing signs of anaphylaxis (lip/tongue swelling, stridor, breathing difficulty) and when to seek emergency care.
- Discuss patient health goals and priorities:
  • Primary goal: reassurance and management of current sting reaction.
- Assess eligibility for GP Management Plan (GPMP) or Team Care Arrangements (TCA): Not discussed.
- Referral to allied health, Quitline, AOD services, Aboriginal health worker, or social supports: Not indicated at this visit.
- Schedule follow-up and recall appointments as needed:
  • Advised to re-contact GP service or attend Emergency Department if symptoms worsen (e.g., airway compromise, spreading erythema, systemic symptoms).

Consider

- Mental health support or counselling referral: Consider if anxiety/panic attacks become more frequent or impact function.
- Specialist referral for complex chronic disease management: Not indicated.
- Dental referral if oral health issues identified: Not indicated.
- Optometry referral for visual concerns or regular screening: Not indicated.
- Audiometry referral if hearing issues suspected: Not indicated.
- Social work or housing support referral if social determinants affect health: Not indicated.

Quality checks

● Missing but clinically expected elements: vitals, anthropometrics, comprehensive lifestyle evaluation, immunisation review, chronic disease screening investigations (blood pressure, glucose, lipids, cancer screening).  
● Internal conflicts or contradictions: Patient reported mild breathing difficulty; clinician observed normal respiration (conflict noted but resolved by clinical judgment of no acute airway compromise).  
● Transcript quality notes: Audio clear; complete dialogue; limited to acute issue, therefore many preventive health components not covered.
